transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I think dispatch and compliance at work have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. There are also little comments on the radio that feel like they’re about me. People say it’s just normal oversight, but I can tell some of the other drivers are reporting on what I’m doing.
Do you think these comments on the radio are actually about you, or is it just a feeling you have?

I think they’re actually about me. I mean, I know it sounds like it could just be regular radio chatter, but the timing and the way they say things line up with my route changes. And with dispatch and compliance seeing everything in the system, it feels like certain drivers are reporting on me too.
Do you think anyone else is in on this, or is it just the people at work who are tracking you?

Mostly it feels like people at work. Dispatch and compliance can see the route changes in the system, and then there are comments on the radio that seem to line up with what I’m doing. I’m not sure about people outside of work, but certain drivers, yeah, I think they’re reporting on me.
Do you think the comments on the radio are meant to convey a specific message about you to others, or are they just discussing your work performance?

It feels more like they’re sending a message about me, not just talking about performance. Like when I make a route change, then something comes over the radio that sounds small, but it lines up too closely. I think dispatch and compliance can see it in the system, and certain drivers are kind of reporting on me through those comments.
Do you believe these comments on the radio are specifically about you, or could they be about someone else or something unrelated to you?

I believe they’re specifically about me. I know people say it could just be normal oversight or random radio talk, but it lines up with my route changes too closely. Dispatch and compliance can see what I’m doing in the computer system, and I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me through those comments.
Do you think the comments on the radio are meant for anyone else to hear, or are they specifically trying to communicate something to you?

I think it’s both, kind of. The comments are on the radio, so other people can hear them, but it feels like they’re aimed at me too. Like they’re letting me know they see what I’m doing with my route changes. Dispatch and compliance can track it in the system, and certain drivers seem like they’re reporting on me through those little comments.
If someone showed you proof that the comments on the radio were not about you, would you believe them?

I’d try to look at it, but honestly I don’t know if I’d believe it right away. Even when people tell me it’s just normal oversight, it still feels too connected to my route changes. Dispatch and compliance can see it in the system, and certain drivers’ comments on the radio just line up too much for me to think it’s nothing.
Would your belief about being tracked change if your coworkers or supervisors told you directly that they are not monitoring your activities?

I don’t think it would change much, at least not right away. They could say they’re not monitoring me, but dispatch and compliance have access to the computer system, and the comments on the radio still match up with my route changes. So I’d feel like maybe they’re just not admitting it, or certain drivers are still reporting on me.
Why do you think dispatch, compliance, and certain drivers are tracking your route changes?

I think it’s because they can see when I change my route in the computer system, and then the radio comments come right after, like they’re pointing it out. It doesn’t feel random to me. Certain drivers seem to know what I’m doing and kind of report on it in those little comments. People say it’s just normal oversight, but it feels more direct than that, like they’re watching what I’m doing.
Have you found any evidence to support your belief that you're being tracked at work?

The evidence I have is mostly what I notice happening at work. Like, I change my route in the system, and then soon after there are little comments on the radio that sound like they’re about that change. It keeps lining up that way. Dispatch and compliance can see the computer system, so to me it feels like certain drivers are reporting on what I’m doing, even if other people say it’s just normal oversight.
Even if you were shown proof that no one is tracking you, do you think you could stop believing that they are?

Honestly, I don’t know if I could stop believing it right away. Even if someone showed me something, I’d still think about the route changes showing up in the computer and then those little radio comments happening after. It feels too connected to just drop it. Maybe I’d try to consider it, but part of me would still feel like dispatch, compliance, or certain drivers are watching and reporting on me.
If you were given absolute proof that no one is tracking you at work, could you then believe that you're not being tracked?

I mean… if it was absolute proof, I’d try to believe it. But honestly, I think I’d still have a hard time letting it go, because I’ve seen how my route changes show up in the computer and then those radio comments happen after. It feels like dispatch and compliance can see it, and certain drivers are reporting on me. So even with proof, part of me would still question it.

Do you think your belief about being tracked would change if everyone at work, including dispatch and compliance, told you directly that they are not monitoring your activities and there's no reason for them to do so?

I think I’d still have trouble changing my mind, honestly. If everyone said they weren’t watching me, I’d hear that, but it wouldn’t erase what I’ve noticed—my route changes in the computer, then those little radio comments after. It just feels too connected. So I might wonder why they’re all saying that, but I’d still feel like dispatch, compliance, or certain drivers are keeping tabs on me.
Do you think your beliefs about being tracked would change if you were alone at work with no one else around to monitor you?

Probably not completely. If I was alone right then, maybe I’d feel a little less watched in that moment, but the computer system would still be there. My route changes still show up, and later there could still be comments on the radio or certain drivers saying things. So I don’t think being alone would really make me stop believing dispatch or compliance are tracking it.
Would your belief about being tracked at work change at all if you were to leave your job and no longer have access to the computer system or radio communications?

If I left the job, I think it might quiet down some because I wouldn’t be seeing the computer or hearing the radio comments anymore. But I don’t know if it would make me stop believing it happened. To me, the route changes and the comments were connected, and it felt like dispatch, compliance, and some drivers were keeping track of me. So leaving might take me away from it, but I’d still probably wonder about it.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your belief about being tracked might not be based in reality?

I’ve considered it, yeah, because people keep telling me it’s just normal oversight. But when I see my route changes in the computer and then hear little comments on the radio after, it feels connected. I can’t just write that off. It really seems like dispatch, compliance, and certain drivers are tracking me or reporting on what I’m doing.
Do you think your belief about being tracked would change if a technical expert showed you how the computer system and radio communications actually work?

Maybe a little, if they really explained it clearly. I’d listen. But I don’t think it would completely change what I believe, because it’s not just the computer by itself. It’s the route changes showing up and then those little comments on the radio, and certain drivers seeming like they know what I’m doing. So even if an expert said it’s normal oversight, I’d still feel like dispatch and compliance are tracking me somehow.
Do you think your beliefs about being tracked would change if you were given absolute proof that they are not true?

If it was really absolute proof, I guess I’d have to think about it. I’m not trying to ignore facts. But it’s hard for me to imagine proof that would explain all of it — the route changes in the computer, the radio comments, and certain drivers seeming like they’re reporting on me. So I might listen, but I don’t know if it would make the feeling go away right away.
